_: Pins what no rule can settle. A null blocks a form outright.
stage.py, reconcile.py and build-pack.py all apply this. In es-ni they
used to disagree, and a warm-up card turned on which one had been right.
Keys starting with _ are notes, not forms.
_crème: Written lower case inside 'ein Kaffee crème', which is how Switzerland
spells it, and capitalised when it stands alone as the order.
_gehört: Ambiguous by spelling: it is hören's participle AND gehören's third
person. All three places the course writes it, it is gehören - the money
belongs to me, the lake belongs to four cantons, both belong to it now.
Revisit when phase 2 brings the perfect tense in and hat gehört starts
appearing; at that point the honest answer may be to block it instead.
_möchte: moechte is genuinely moegen's Konjunktiv II, and forms.py states it as
such - which is correct German and the wrong answer to give a learner.
The course teaches moechten as its own word, the polite want, so tapping
moechte has to say would like rather than to like.
